title: Variant parity compatibility matrix refresh for regional/tier routing
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Context: Smart routing will automatically fall back to compatible model variants across regions/tier levels when capacity is constrained. We need an authoritative, machine-readable compatibility matrix covering tokenizer parity, context-length compatibility, tooling/function-calling parity, streaming semantics, and KV-cache compatibility so routing policies can make safe fallback choices. Goal: refresh and extend the existing compatibility matrix, add automated parity checks, and integrate a gating rule in the router to only allow fallbacks to variants that meet the critical compatibility requirements.

Scope: tokenizer compatibility (token ids, special tokens, merges/vocab changes), context / max-seq parity and expected truncation behavior, function/tool-calling signature parity (arg shapes, JSON schema stability), streaming and incremental output compatibility (chunk boundaries + eos behavior), KV cache layout/versioning hints (forward/backwards compatibility), and SDK/console integration flags.

Deliverables:
- Updated CSV/JSON compatibility matrix schema and canonical columns (tokenizer_hash, tokenizer_version, pad_behavior, supports_function_calls, streaming_semantics, kv_cache_compat, max_context_tokens, quantization_notes, model_variant_tags).
- Automated test harness that runs tokenization diffs + sample tool-calling end-to-end smoke tests for each model variant on a nightly cadence.
- Repository of canonical test prompts and function schemas for regen and validation.
- Router integration change: routing policy rule that consults the matrix and only permits fallbacks when 'critical_checks' pass (tokenizer + function-calling + context >= requested length).
- Documentation page (Confluence) and a dashboard tile in Console showing matrix health and recent parity test failures.

Constraints & trade-offs: Conservative gating reduces available fallback targets (may increase error surface under heavy load) but prevents subtle correctness regressions (mismatched tokenization or tool-calling shapes). A staged rollout is required: start with permissive logging-only mode for 2 weeks, then enable hard gating for low-latency endpoints, and expand to all routes after validation.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement model patching or tokenizer rewriting; it focuses on detection, documentation, and routing gating only.

2026-02-24 - Design review (MJ): UX note: Console should surface "reason why fallback denied" with human-readable tags (e.g., tokenizer_mismatch, missing_function_support). Keep messaging short to avoid exposing internal model details. Design suggested a small icon and tooltip for matrix status in the route editor.

2026-02-26 - ENG: Implemented nightly GitHub Actions job that runs tokenization parity and uploads a JSON report to object storage (s3://redwood-compat/reports/). PR #281 open for review: github.com/redwood-inference/compat-tests/pull/281

2026-03-01 - BT: Integrated 'critical_checks' evaluation that marks a variant 'fallback_allowed' if tokenization parity + function-calling parity + context_capacity_check pass. Running in logging-only mode for routes tagged 'experimental-fallbacks'.

2026-03-04 - QA (SR): End-to-end function-calling smoke tests added. Found a mismatch in function arg ordering for variant 'x-stable-v2-qa' causing tool calls to fail in 0.3% of cases.
